newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe's cash cocoa routine, industry well covered.
newsitem.headline: Europe's cash cocoa routine, industry well covered.

text.p: Europe's cash cocoa trade had been pruned to routine levels by late this week with many market players on holiday and industry reported to be well covered, dealers said on Friday.
"We've seen the normal two-way trade but volumes have tailed off," one trader in continental Europe said.
Earlier in the week business was reported to be a little more active, with Ghana and Ivory Coast offering beans into the physical market for new crop positions and beyond.

Traders said the chocolate industry had been building up cover in the past few weeks, but was becoming more confident that prices might have reached a peak. It had filled most gaps in its requirements.
German chocolate buyers in particular were reported to have been very active on market dips on Monday and Tuesday.
"Those that missed the market earlier this year thought now is time to rectify this and came rushing in. There was quite a lot of industrial buying done," one trader said.
Spot Ivory Coast cocoa was reported to be trading between five and 10 stg under the September terminal position for high quality beans and up to 35 stg under for lower grades.
But the heavy buying only really lasted two days.

Slack physical volumes on Friday were reflected in slow trade on the London futures market, where the benchmark September contract had slipped 12 stg to 1,043 stg a tonne by mid-afternoon amid a turnover of just 1,021 lots.
Trade sources in Europe continued to report quality problems with Ivorian deliveries, which had increased the reluctance of some to take on fresh purchases from Abidjan.
The fundamental outlook for cocoa was boosted earlier this week by higher-than-expected second quarter grinds in the major processing centres of the Netherlands, Germany and the UK.
The Dutch figure, the largest in the world, was up more than 10 percent on the previous year's quarter and the German and UK totals, although down, were stronger than expected.
